findings.title: `-ms-align-items` is not a valid CSS property
findings.body: The `align-items` mixin outputs `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` which is not a real CSS property in any version of Internet Explorer or Edge. The correct legacy IE property is `-ms-flex-align` (already included on line 120). This line is dead code that will be silently ignored by all browsers, but it indicates a misunderstanding that could lead to confusion. It should be removed.

findings.title: `order` mixin does not account for 1-based indexing of legacy box-ordinal-group
findings.body: The `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties are 1-indexed (first item is group 1), while the modern `order` property is 0-indexed (first item is order 0). The mixin passes `$val` directly to both, so `@include order(3)` produces `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 3` which places the element in the 3rd position in old browsers but the 4th position (after items with order 0, 1, 2) in modern browsers. On older WebKit/Mozilla browsers that only support the old box model, `.panel` in the header will appear one position earlier than intended. The mixin should add 1 to the value for the old ordinal-group properties.

findings.title: Removal of `.title { float: left }` may break header layout
findings.body: The diff removes the `.title { float: left; }` rule from `.d-header`. While `.contents` is now a flex container (which handles child positioning), the `.title` class is still used in header markup. If any child of `.d-header` outside `.contents` uses the `.title` class, or if there are plugins/themes that rely on `.d-header .title` being floated, this removal could cause a layout regression. The PR provides no replacement styling for `.title` elements.

findings.title: `align-items` mixin does not map modern values to legacy equivalents
findings.body: The mixin passes `$alignment` directly to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which only accept `start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline`, `stretch` — not the modern `flex-start` or `flex-end` values. While current usages (`center`, `baseline`) happen to be valid in both syntaxes, the mixin will silently produce invalid CSS if called with `flex-start` or `flex-end` in the future. A proper implementation should map `flex-start` → `start` and `flex-end` → `end` for the legacy properties.
